findings.issue_text: Synchronous full-feed processing inside a single-URL retrieval job — RetrieveTopic Sidekiq job calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously, fetching the entire RSS/Atom feed and importing every item inline just to find one URL
Unbounded RSS feed item iteration with no limit or batching — every feed item is processed in a single pass with no cap on count, no pagination, no backpressure, and no way to resume

No timeout or size limit on remote HTTP fetches — open(url) calls have no read_timeout, open_timeout, or max-size check, risking indefinite blocking of the Sidekiq worker and memory exhaustion from large responses
Potential N+1 query for post authors in embed view — each post in the iteration accesses post.user without visible preloading of user associations
Feed cache key defined but never used — feed_key is intended for conditional fetching (Last-Modified/ETag) but never called, causing unnecessary HTTP fetches and per-item DB lookups on every poll
SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) uses open-uri with no open_timeout/read_timeout, allowing a slow feed host to stall the Sidekiq worker indefinitely
Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...) in import_remote has no timeout, allowing an unresponsive embed URL to hang the worker with no upper bound
i.content.scrub assumes every RSS/Atom item exposes content, but SimpleRSS returns nil for missing elements, causing nil.scrub to raise NoMethodError and abort the entire hourly poll
rss.items.each has no per-item rescue, so a single bad item aborts processing of every remaining item in the feed, suppressing all subsequent legitimate entries
sidekiq_options retry: false combined with no exception handling means transient failures silently kill the poll with no retry, no notification, and no visibility

Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) runs the entire feed poll synchronously inside the retrieve_topic worker, and Sidekiq's default 25 retries amplify upstream load and re-hit the same hang if PollFeed raises or hangs
<%- end if %> in embed/best.html.erb is not valid Ruby in ERB, causing the template to fail to compile and return a 500 for every best render where a topic already exists
TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) is unguarded against trashed/deleted topics, causing a 500 instead of falling back to the loading/retrieve path
embed.post is dereferenced without a nil check before PostRevisor.new(post), causing NoMethodError if the embedded post was deleted but the topic_embeds row remains

The 30-second document.location.reload() loop in loading.html.erb has no max-retry or abort condition, causing indefinite client reloads if the retrieve_topic job fails permanently, with no failure surfaced to the viewer
Tests for 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' pass for the wrong reason — feed_polling_enabled? defaults to false, so poll_feed is never called regardless of stubbed values
Core poll_feed logic (RSS parsing, item iteration, URL extraction, content escaping, TopicEmbed.import call) is never exercised in any test
EmbedController spec mocks wrong layer — tests TopicRetriever internals instead of verifying controller's actual responsibility of enqueuing a job with correct arguments
perform_retrieve and retrieved_recently? are stubbed and never exercised — Redis throttle logic and retrieve flow are untested
No test for TopicEmbed.import_remote — network fetching, readability parsing, and title extraction are untested
No test for Jobs::RetrieveTopic — argument extraction, user lookup, and no_throttle for staff are untested
No test for EmbedController#ensure_embedable URI::InvalidURIError rescue clause — invalid referer URI path is not covered
No view tests for best.html.erb / loading.html.erb — potential syntax error in template goes undetected because views are never rendered
No edge-case tests for TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls — already-absolute URLs, protocol-relative URLs, custom ports, and empty/nil attributes are untested
Test named 'is 404' only asserts response.should_not be_success — doesn't verify status code and would pass for 400 or 500
No direct unit test for Post#cook raw_html branch — only indirectly tested through TopicEmbed.import
No direct test for PostRevisor#revise! with skip_validations — validation bypass behavior only indirectly tested
`<%- end if %>` is invalid ERB/Ruby; `end` cannot take an `if` modifier, causing a SyntaxError that breaks the entire embed feature
`feed_key` is defined and memoized but never called anywhere, making it dead code
`require_dependency 'email/sender'` in RetrieveTopic is unused and misleadingly suggests email work
`embed_by_username` user lookup is duplicated in both TopicRetriever and PollFeed with duplicated blank-handling logic that should be centralized
Scheduled job's `execute` is called synchronously via `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, tightly coupling TopicRetriever to the job and abusing the job abstraction
`TopicEmbed#import` mutates the caller's `contents` string via `<<`, which callers won't expect and will raise on frozen strings
Embed.js origin check uses `indexOf` substring matching on URL strings instead of comparing normalized origins, risking bypass via scheme/port mismatch or coincidental substring
`postMessage` targetOrigin is derived from unvalidated `request.referer` which can be nil/empty, disabling origin restriction; should use trusted `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`
`<%= raw post.cooked %>` renders unsanitized imported HTML for `cook_method == raw_html`, creating an XSS sink that bypasses the sanitization pipeline
Migration hardcodes `default: 1` coupled to enum ordinal ordering; reordering `cook_methods` would silently change the default meaning
`absolutize_urls` port logic hardcodes 80/443 as universal defaults ignoring scheme, producing wrong prefixes for https-on-80 or http-on-443 URLs
`i.content.scrub` assumes `content` exists but it is nil for many RSS/Atom feeds, raising NoMethodError and killing the entire hourly poll on one bad item
`open(feed_polling_url)` has no error handling and with `retry: false` transient failures are silently swallowed for an hour with no observability
`open(url)` on arbitrary URLs honors non-HTTP schemes like `file://`, creating local-file/SSRF risks; should use an HTTP-only client and reject non-http(s) schemes
Disqus import regression: `import_remote` does not accept `created_at` or `:category` options, so imported topics lose original timestamps and category assignment
Cache/reload mismatch: loading response cached for 60s but reloads after 30s, causing topics available at ~35s to remain hidden until cache expires
`import` method mixes creation and revision in one method with inconsistent transactional boundaries; should be split into separate create/update methods
Using `force: true` on `create_table :top_topics` in an existing migration will silently drop the table and destroy all data if it already exists, with no rollback path to recover erased data
Using `force: true` on `create_table :topic_embeds` will silently destroy any table and data surviving from a failed prior migration attempt, with no way to recover pre-existing data on rollback

Adding `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` causes a full table rewrite with exclusive lock on PostgreSQL < 11 and MySQL, risking significant downtime on the large posts table
Declaring `embed_url` as `string` (varchar 255) may truncate long URLs, and truncation combined with a unique index could cause false uniqueness collisions

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Synchronous full-feed processing inside a single-URL retrieval job — RetrieveTopic Sidekiq job calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously, fetching the entire RSS/Atom feed and importing every item inline just to find one URL

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (synchronously) before attempting `fetch_http`:

```ruby
if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?
  Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})
  return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?
end
```

`Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` then does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items.each` importing every item via `TopicEmbed.import(...)`. This means a single-URL retrieval (triggered via the `RetrieveTopic` job or elsewhere) can synchronously fetch and process the entire feed, which is exactly what the finding describes and is a clear inefficiency/defect risk (latency/work amplification).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded RSS feed item iteration with no limit or batching — every feed item is processed in a single pass with no cap on count, no pagination, no backpressure, and no way to resume

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` parses the entire feed (`rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and then iterates all entries with `rss.items.each do |i| ... TopicEmbed.import(...) end` with no limit, batching, or checkpointing. This makes the job runtime/work proportional to the feed size, and a large feed would be processed in a single execution with no backpressure or resume mechanism beyond per-item de-dupe by `embed_url`/`content_sha1`. The finding accurately describes this behavior as introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No timeout or size limit on remote HTTP fetches — open(url) calls have no read_timeout, open_timeout, or max-size check, risking indefinite blocking of the Sidekiq worker and memory exhaustion from large responses

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple remote fetches using `open-uri` without any timeout or size limiting options. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, it does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`; in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` it does `open(url).read` and passes the full response into `Readability::Document`. Neither call supplies `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` (supported by open-uri) nor any max-size/content-length guard, so a slow/unresponsive server can block the scheduled/regular Sidekiq job indefinitely and a large response can be read fully into memory.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Potential N+1 query for post authors in embed view — each post in the iteration accesses post.user without visible preloading of user associations

adjudication.rationale: The embed view iterates `@topic_view.posts` and calls `post.user`, but the diff does not show how `@topic_view.posts` is loaded. The controller uses `TopicView.new(...)`, and whether that preloads users (thus avoiding N+1) is defined outside this diff. Therefore the finding depends on unseen implementation details and is not a verifiable defect introduced by the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feed cache key defined but never used — feed_key is intended for conditional fetching (Last-Modified/ETag) but never called, causing unnecessary HTTP fetches and per-item DB lookups on every poll

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Jobs::PollFeed` class, a `feed_key` method is defined (building a Redis-style key based on the feed URL), but it is never referenced anywhere in `execute` or `poll_feed`. The implementation always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no conditional request logic (ETag/If-Modified-Since) and then iterates all items, calling `TopicEmbed.import` which does a `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` lookup per item. So the finding that the cache key is defined but unused (and thus conditional fetching is not actually implemented) is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) uses open-uri with no open_timeout/read_timeout, allowing a slow feed host to stall the Sidekiq worker indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed the code does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` after requiring `open-uri`, and it does not pass any `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options. That means the Sidekiq thread executing this scheduled job can be tied up waiting on the remote feed fetch for as long as the underlying HTTP/DNS stack allows (often long/default timeouts), rather than failing fast. The diff clearly introduces this network call without explicit timeouts; the “indefinitely” wording is somewhat strong (Ruby/Net::HTTP has defaults), but the lack of explicit timeouts and potential worker stall is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...) in import_remote has no timeout, allowing an unresponsive embed URL to hang the worker with no upper bound

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `open(url).read` without passing explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options, so it’s true no custom timeout is configured. However, the finding’s stronger claim (“hang the worker with no upper bound”) is not verifiable from the diff because Ruby’s `open-uri`/`Net::HTTP` have default timeouts (e.g., `read_timeout`/`open_timeout` defaults), so it’s not clearly an unbounded hang introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: i.content.scrub assumes every RSS/Atom item exposes content, but SimpleRSS returns nil for missing elements, causing nil.scrub to raise NoMethodError and abort the entire hourly poll
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify that calling `i.content.scrub` can fail because `i.content` may be nil for many RSS/Atom items, leading to a NoMethodError/nil pointer crash. The candidate doesn’t explicitly mention falling back to `description`, but it flags the same root cause and failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: rss.items.each has no per-item rescue, so a single bad item aborts processing of every remaining item in the feed, suppressing all subsequent legitimate entries

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the feed is processed with `rss.items.each do |i| ... TopicEmbed.import(...) end` and there is no `begin/rescue` inside the loop. If any item triggers an exception (e.g., `i.content` is nil and `.scrub` is called, malformed URL handling inside `TopicEmbed.import`, etc.), Ruby will raise and abort the entire `poll_feed` method, preventing remaining items from being processed in that run. This matches the finding’s claim about one bad item stopping subsequent items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sidekiq_options retry: false combined with no exception handling means transient failures silently kill the poll with no retry, no notification, and no visibility

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Jobs::PollFeed` as a scheduled Sidekiq job with `sidekiq_options retry: false` and no `rescue` around network/parse calls (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `SimpleRSS.parse`). It’s true that a transient exception would not be retried by Sidekiq for that execution. However, the finding overstates the impact: a failure would not be “silent” (Sidekiq logs/records job failures), and it would not “kill the poll” permanently because this is a scheduled job (`recurrence { hourly }`) that will run again on the next schedule. Claims about “no notification”/“no visibility” are not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) runs the entire feed poll synchronously inside the retrieve_topic worker, and Sidekiq's default 25 retries amplify upstream load and re-hit the same hang if PollFeed raises or hangs

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly (synchronously) when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to `fetch_http` (see `lib/topic_retriever.rb`). `TopicRetriever` is invoked from the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` worker (`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`), so this makes the retrieve_topic Sidekiq job run the full feed poll inline (including `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterating `rss.items`). If `PollFeed` blocks/raises, it will block/fail the retrieve_topic job; and because retrieve_topic has no `sidekiq_options retry: false` override in the diff, it will use the job system’s default retry behavior (commonly Sidekiq’s default), which can re-run the same synchronous polling repeatedly, amplifying upstream load.

adjudication_records.issue_text: <%- end if %> in embed/best.html.erb is not valid Ruby in ERB, causing the template to fail to compile and return a 500 for every best render where a topic already exists
TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) is unguarded against trashed/deleted topics, causing a 500 instead of falling back to the loading/retrieve path

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the code does unconditionally call `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` returns an id, and `topic_id_for_embed` does not validate that the referenced topic exists or is not deleted. However, the proposed finding specifically claims this will "cause a 500" for trashed/deleted topics and that it should "fall back" to the loading/retrieve path. Whether `TopicView.new` raises on deleted/trashed topics (or handles them gracefully) is not shown in this diff, so the 500 behavior and the need for fallback are not verifiable from the changes provided.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.post is dereferenced without a nil check before PostRevisor.new(post), causing NoMethodError if the embedded post was deleted but the topic_embeds row remains

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an existing embed is found it does `post = embed.post` and, if the content hash changed, unconditionally does `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)`. If the associated Post record was deleted (no DB foreign key is shown; `post_id` is just an integer with `null: false`), `embed.post` will be `nil`, so `PostRevisor.new(nil)` (and later `revise!`) will raise at runtime. There is no nil check or recovery path (e.g., recreate the post/embed), so the finding describes a real defect path in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 30-second document.location.reload() loop in loading.html.erb has no max-retry or abort condition, causing indefinite client reloads if the retrieve_topic job fails permanently, with no failure surfaced to the viewer

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/loading.html.erb the only behavior is a JS timer that calls `document.location.reload()` every 30000ms with no counter, timeout, or failure UI. In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. If the job fails permanently (e.g., invalid URL, network error, host check preventing retrieval, feed polling disabled, etc.), the controller will keep rendering `loading`, so the client will reload indefinitely and never surface an error state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests for 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' pass for the wrong reason — feed_polling_enabled? defaults to false, so poll_feed is never called regardless of stubbed values

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#execute`, `poll_feed` is only called if `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? && SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? && SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?`. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the tests "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" stub only `feed_polling_url` or `embed_by_username` to `nil`, but do not stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to `true`. Since the default for `feed_polling_enabled` is `false` (added in `config/site_settings.yml` in this diff), the guard short-circuits on `feed_polling_enabled?` and `poll_feed` will never be called regardless of the other stubs. Thus those tests can pass even if the code did not check `feed_polling_url` / `embed_by_username`, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Core poll_feed logic (RSS parsing, item iteration, URL extraction, content escaping, TopicEmbed.import call) is never exercised in any test

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed with substantial logic (SimpleRSS.parse(open(...)), iterating rss.items, URL normalization, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), and TopicEmbed.import). The only added test (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb) verifies that execute() gates and calls poll_feed, but it never invokes poll_feed itself nor stubs/parses an RSS feed to exercise item iteration or the TopicEmbed.import calls. No other specs in the diff reference Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed. So the core poll_feed behavior is indeed untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController spec mocks wrong layer — tests TopicRetriever internals instead of verifying controller's actual responsibility of enqueuing a job with correct arguments

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding is verifiably correct. In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`; it does not instantiate or call `TopicRetriever` at all. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` has a test (`"tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found"`) that expects `TopicRetriever.new` to be called and `retriever.retrieve` to run. This spec is testing a layer that the controller does not use, so it is incorrect and would fail against the code in the diff; it also fails to verify the controller’s actual behavior (enqueuing the job with correct args).

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_retrieve and retrieved_recently? are stubbed and never exercised — Redis throttle logic and retrieve flow are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce Redis throttling logic in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` and a multi-step retrieve flow (`perform_retrieve` -> PollFeed -> `fetch_http`). The added spec (`spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`) stubs `retrieved_recently?` to return true/false and only asserts whether `perform_retrieve` is invoked; it never executes the real Redis logic or the real retrieve flow. However, this is a test coverage gap rather than a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect in the production code introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for TopicEmbed.import_remote — network fetching, readability parsing, and title extraction are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`) which performs `open(url).read` network fetching and runs `Readability::Document` to extract `doc.title` and `doc.content`, but the added specs only cover `TopicEmbed.import` (see `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`) and do not exercise `import_remote` at all. There is also no other spec referencing `import_remote`, despite it being used by `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and the Disqus thor task. So the finding that this behavior is untested is accurate and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for Jobs::RetrieveTopic — argument extraction, user lookup, and no_throttle for staff are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`) but does not add any corresponding spec file that exercises its behavior (argument validation, optional user lookup, and passing `no_throttle` based on `staff?`). However, this is a test coverage request rather than a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for EmbedController#ensure_embedable URI::InvalidURIError rescue clause — invalid referer URI path is not covered

adjudication.rationale: EmbedController#ensure_embeddable explicitly rescues URI::InvalidURIError when parsing `URI(request.referer || '')`, but the added controller specs only cover (1) missing embed_url, (2) missing embeddable_host, (3) no referer (nil/blank), and (4) a valid referer. There is no spec that stubs `request.referer` to an invalid URI string that would trigger URI::InvalidURIError and exercise the rescue clause, so that path is not covered by tests introduced in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No view tests for best.html.erb / loading.html.erb — potential syntax error in template goes undetected because views are never rendered

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new templates (best.html.erb, loading.html.erb) but no explicit view specs. However, the proposed issue is about test coverage (“potential syntax error goes undetected”), not a verifiable defect in the production code introduced by the diff. Also, while the new controller spec calls `get :best`, RSpec controller specs do not render views by default unless `render_views` is enabled, so it’s true the templates aren’t exercised—but that’s a testing-gap suggestion rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness problem shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No edge-case tests for TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls — already-absolute URLs, protocol-relative URLs, custom ports, and empty/nil attributes are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` and adds a spec that only asserts conversion of relative `href`/`src` values starting with `/` into absolute URLs. There are no tests covering already-absolute URLs, protocol-relative URLs (`//...`), custom port handling, or nil/empty attributes. However, this is a test-coverage suggestion rather than a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect in the introduced code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test named 'is 404' only asserts response.should_not be_success — doesn't verify status code and would pass for 400 or 500

adjudication.rationale:
In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the example named `"is 404 without an embed_url"` only does:

```rb
get :best
response.should_not be_success
```

This asserts merely that the response is not in the 2xx range; it does not verify that the status is specifically 404. The spec would still pass if the controller returned 400, 401/403, 500, etc. So the test name/intent (“is 404”) is not actually enforced by the assertion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No direct unit test for Post#cook raw_html branch — only indirectly tested through TopicEmbed.import

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `Post#cook` early return for `raw_html`. While there isn’t a unit test that calls `Post#cook` directly, `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` asserts `post.cooked == post.raw` when `post.cook_method` is `raw_html`, which exercises the behavior through the normal creation path. This is a test-coverage/granularity comment rather than a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No direct test for PostRevisor#revise! with skip_validations — validation bypass behavior only indirectly tested

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` to call `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, adding a validation-bypass capability. The added/updated specs (e.g., `TopicEmbed` update path) invoke `revise!` with `skip_validations: true`, but they don’t assert that validations were actually bypassed (e.g., by forcing a validation failure and confirming the revise still succeeds). However, this is a test coverage observation, not a verifiable bug/correctness defect introduced by the diff itself—the code can still be correct without a direct test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `<%- end if %>` is invalid ERB/Ruby; `end` cannot take an `if` modifier, causing a SyntaxError that breaks the entire embed feature
matched_golden_ids: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same syntax bug: the ERB/Ruby block is closed with `end if`, which is invalid and will cause a SyntaxError during rendering; it should be just `end` to close the `if` block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `feed_key` is defined and memoized but never called anywhere, making it dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` is defined and memoized (`@feed_key ||= ...`) but nothing in the diff calls `feed_key` (neither `execute` nor `poll_feed` nor any other added code references it). This makes it unused/dead code as introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `require_dependency 'email/sender'` in RetrieveTopic is unused and misleadingly suggests email work

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is not referenced anywhere in the job’s code; the job only looks up a user and calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`. However, this is primarily an unused/dead require (a cleanliness/clarity nit) rather than a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff, since it doesn’t change behavior in an obviously broken way.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `embed_by_username` user lookup is duplicated in both TopicRetriever and PollFeed with duplicated blank-handling logic that should be centralized

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show duplicated logic: both `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` and `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` perform `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and return early if the user is blank. However, this is a maintainability/style concern (DRY) rather than a verifiable bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the change. The duplication does not cause incorrect behavior in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Scheduled job's `execute` is called synchronously via `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, tightly coupling TopicRetriever to the job and abusing the job abstraction

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. However, this is not a clear bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the change: `TopicRetriever` itself is invoked from the background job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (enqueued by `EmbedController#best`), so the synchronous execution still happens off the request thread. While this may be an architectural/design concern (job abstraction/coupling), the finding frames it as an “abuse” rather than demonstrating a verifiable malfunction or incorrect behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `TopicEmbed#import` mutates the caller's `contents` string via `<<`, which callers won't expect and will raise on frozen strings

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends directly to the `contents` argument, which mutates the caller-provided String in-place. This is verifiable in the diff and can cause unintended side effects if the caller expects `contents` to remain unchanged or reuses it later. It will also raise (FrozenError in modern Ruby) if a caller passes a frozen string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed.js origin check uses `indexOf` substring matching on URL strings instead of comparing normalized origins, risking bypass via scheme/port mismatch or coincidental substring
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden and candidate issues flag the same underlying vulnerability: origin validation is done with `indexOf`/substring matching on URL strings, which can be bypassed by crafted domains containing the trusted domain as a substring (e.g., `evil-discourseUrl.com`). The candidate also notes normalization concerns (scheme/port), but still centers on the same flawed substring check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `postMessage` targetOrigin is derived from unvalidated `request.referer` which can be nil/empty, disabling origin restriction; should use trusted `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`
`<%= raw post.cooked %>` renders unsanitized imported HTML for `cook_method == raw_html`, creating an XSS sink that bypasses the sanitization pipeline

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method == :raw_html` path in `Post#cook` that returns `raw` directly, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` and `Jobs::PollFeed` feed untrusted HTML (`i.content` from an external RSS/ATOM URL, only `CGI.unescapeHTML` + `scrub`) into `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the content is then output via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which will emit that imported HTML without sanitization. Since `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `href/src` and does not strip scripts/unsafe attributes, this is a verifiable XSS sink introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration hardcodes `default: 1` coupled to enum ordinal ordering; reordering `cook_methods` would silently change the default meaning

adjudication.rationale: The migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` adds `cook_method` as an integer with `default: 1`, and the enum is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`. In this diff there is no evidence that `1` is incorrect (it likely corresponds to `:regular`, consistent with common Discourse enum conventions). The proposed issue only manifests if someone later reorders the enum values, which is a hypothetical future change rather than a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `absolutize_urls` port logic hardcodes 80/443 as universal defaults ignoring scheme, producing wrong prefixes for https-on-80 or http-on-443 URLs

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the prefix is built as `scheme://host` and then the port is appended only if `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`. This treats 80 and 443 as “always default” regardless of scheme. For uncommon but valid URLs like `https://example.com:80/...` or `http://example.com:443/...`, the code will incorrectly omit the explicit port, producing a different origin/prefix than the input URL, and thus generate wrong absolute URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `i.content.scrub` assumes `content` exists but it is nil for many RSS/Atom feeds, raising NoMethodError and killing the entire hourly poll on one bad item

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If an RSS/Atom item lacks a `content` field (common; many feeds only provide `description`/`summary`), then `i.content` will be `nil` and calling `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire `poll_feed` run on that item.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `open(feed_polling_url)` has no error handling and with `retry: false` transient failures are silently swallowed for an hour with no observability

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` performs a network read via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no `rescue`/logging around it. Any transient `open-uri`/HTTP/parse error will raise and fail the scheduled job, and because the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, Sidekiq will not retry the failed run (so the next attempt will only happen on the next hourly recurrence). The "silently swallowed"/"no observability" part isn’t strictly evidenced in the diff (Sidekiq typically logs exceptions), but the lack of error handling combined with `retry: false` causing missed polling until the next schedule is directly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `open(url)` on arbitrary URLs honors non-HTTP schemes like `file://`, creating local-file/SSRF risks; should use an HTTP-only client and reject non-http(s) schemes
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that calling `open` on a user/attacker-controlled URL without validation allows server-side requests to arbitrary targets (SSRF). The candidate additionally notes non-HTTP schemes like `file://`, but it’s the same core issue: unvalidated URL fetching via `open`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import regression: `import_remote` does not accept `created_at` or `:category` options, so imported topics lose original timestamps and category assignment

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Disqus importer to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` instead of `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` only uses `opts[:title]` and then calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which in turn calls `PostCreator.new` without `created_at` or `category`. Additionally, the CLI option `:category` and the code that computed `category_id` were removed. As a result, imported Disqus topics/posts will be created with default timestamps (current time) and without category assignment, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache/reload mismatch: loading response cached for 60s but reloads after 30s, causing topics available at ~35s to remain hidden until cache expires

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, the else branch renders the `loading` template when no topic_id is found, but the method still executes `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` afterward. That sets cache headers for 60s even for the loading page. Meanwhile `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` runs `document.location.reload()` after 30s. If the browser/proxy honors the 60s cache (max-age), the 30s reload can be satisfied from cache and not hit the server, so a topic that becomes available shortly after (e.g., at ~35s) may not be shown until the cached loading response expires (~60s). This mismatch is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `import` method mixes creation and revision in one method with inconsistent transactional boundaries; should be split into separate create/update methods

adjudication.rationale:
The diff’s `TopicEmbed.import` intentionally handles two cases: create-on-first-seen (`embed.blank?`) and update-on-change (existing `embed`). The proposed finding is primarily a refactoring/design suggestion (“should be split”), not a clear defect.

While it’s true the create path is wrapped in a `Topic.transaction` and the update path is not, the diff does not show any concrete incorrect behavior stemming from that. The update path calls `PostRevisor#revise!` and then updates `content_sha1`; there’s no verifiable bug in the diff proving that lack of a transaction causes inconsistency or failure. This is speculative rather than a demonstrable problem introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Using `force: true` on `create_table :top_topics` in an existing migration will silently drop the table and destroy all data if it already exists, with no rollback path to recover erased data

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In ActiveRecord, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before creating it, which would erase all existing `top_topics` data without any way for the migration rollback to restore that lost data. While migrations normally run only once, this is still a real, verifiable destructive behavior introduced by the diff if the migration is executed in an environment where `top_topics` already exists (e.g., table created manually/out-of-band, or other atypical migration history).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Using `force: true` on `create_table :topic_embeds` will silently destroy any table and data surviving from a failed prior migration attempt, with no way to recover pre-existing data on rollback

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which in Rails will drop the table if it already exists and then recreate it. That is a destructive operation that can silently wipe any pre-existing `topic_embeds` data (e.g., if the table was created by a prior/failed run, manual setup, or partial deploy) and there is no rollback path to restore that wiped data. This behavior is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` causes a full table rewrite with exclusive lock on PostgreSQL < 11 and MySQL, risking significant downtime on the large posts table

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-null default is implemented by rewriting the whole table, which takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration; similarly many MySQL/InnoDB versions perform a table rebuild/copy for this pattern. Given `posts` is typically a very large table in Discourse, this migration can cause significant blocking/downtime during deploy. This risk is directly introduced by the shown migration definition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Declaring `embed_url` as `string` (varchar 255) may truncate long URLs, and truncation combined with a unique index could cause false uniqueness collisions

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`, `embed_url` is created as `t.string :embed_url` with no explicit `limit`, which in Rails maps to `varchar(255)` on common DBs. URLs can exceed 255 characters; on PostgreSQL this would cause insert/update failures, and on databases that truncate (or where truncation can occur via encoding/adapter behavior), the subsequent `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true` could produce false uniqueness collisions because different long URLs may share the same first 255 chars. This is directly introduced by the diff (new table + unique index).
